page: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a bare metal server configured with an AMD EPYC 4345P processor featuring 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.9 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the CPU includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions. The system is equipped with 123.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing approximately 7.71 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 3890 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tasks scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance, including Passmark CPU and multi-threaded stress-ng tests, falls within the average tier. Memory performance is mixed; while the Passmark memory score ranks in the top 10% and small-block cached read bandwidth is average, large-block uncached write bandwidth is weak, landing in the bottom 25%. For language model workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds for small 135M models, but drops to average speeds when processing larger 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal configuration offers high resource density by combining dedicated EPYC compute cores with a substantial 3.8 TB NVMe storage array and DDR5 memory. The primary tradeoff is the lower multi-core scaling and weaker uncached memory write speeds relative to its strong single-core capabilities. This hardware profile is appropriate for workloads requiring high single-threaded CPU throughput and fast local storage access, such as relational databases, text and image processing pipelines, static web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference.
